124.t: How Ella Fitzgerald came into Chick Webb's band
124.s: Chick picked Ella from the Apollo amateur show while McRae was away with Lil Armstrong; she was in the band six months before him.
124.ch: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
124.q: I -- remember I'm coming in from Buffalo. I left Lil. I was there on the road with Lil Armstrong. We came in that winter to play the Apollo Theater. I think that winter, here in New York with Chick, it was an amateur show going on. That's when they heard Ella.

124.t: Chick Webb's move to broaden the band; McRae as straw boss
124.s: After the road trip the band had money from one-nighters and McRae took over details for Webb, picking music for Ella.
124.ch: With Chick Webb and Ella Fitzgerald, 1936-39
124.q: This is like -- I think we had this down some place on the paper (Inaudible). We was just talking about the -- Unless you want to go back into the Chick Webb thing.

124.t: Bardu Ali, the front man of Chick's band
124.s: Bardu Ali fronted the band as a showman and dancer; later Babe Wallace fronted it before Benny Carter declined to take over.
124.ch: With Chick Webb and Ella Fitzgerald, 1936-39
124.q: All right, like a Lucky Millinder. He was flashy like Lucky Millinder, but not as flashy as Mike Lucky. Lucky would go way out, you know. Jump off the piano and jump down and do a split -- all that kind of stuff -- with his tails on. Bardu Ali could do a split, turn over, and do all the things like…

124.t: How McRae came to lead the band after Webb's death
124.s: The band played Chicago and New York dates, and when Benny Carter wanted Ella as his own, Moe Gale gave the band to McRae.
124.ch: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
124.q: -- when we played, I told you we played about four dates out in New York. We were in Pittsburgh. I mean, Pittsburgh was the first big date that we jumped off to after we left the Savoy Ballroom. You know, we went back to the Savoy Ballroom to tune the band up -- to get the band into shape.

124.t: Ella hands over the baton; Elmer Williams rejoins
124.s: In Chicago, Ella told McRae to lead the band, Babe Wallace had disappeared, and Elmer Williams borrowed a tenor from Coleman Hawkins.
124.ch: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
124.q: : We went to Pittsburgh and (inaudible) through the middle west and (inaudible). We was on our way to (inaudible). We were working -- we were doing one nighters heading into Chicago (inaudible). We played a theater out there. Colored

31.t: Director of music at the Lafayette and Apollo, and discovering Ella and Sarah Vaughan
31.s: He becomes theatre music director in 1930, claims to have discovered Ella Fitzgerald for Chick Webb and Sarah Vaughan for Earl Hines, and lists big bands at the Apollo.
31.ch: Coming up in New York and Harlem theatres
31.q: I went with -- I'm ahead of the story but in 1930, I went into the theatre, see, director of music. At the Lafayette, we went from the Lafayette into the Harlem Opera House, that's when I discovered Ella Fitzgerald and I introduced her to Chick Webb. Chick Webb exploit her, but I discovered her.

31.t: Moving to the Apollo and introducing Ella to Chick Webb
31.s: Whaley recalls the Apollo's productive era, amateur night, and repeats how he introduced Ella Fitzgerald to Chick Webb.
31.ch: Apollo years, Eubie Blake and failing eyesight
31.q: We were talking about the Apollo Theatre, see, I went there from the Lafayette into the Opera House in '30 and went into the Apollo Theatre, I think it's in '31. Now, all the big bands came in there and that was an era of productivity, oh, they were beautiful see, all new bands would come along and…

251.s: Albert regrets declining Ella Fitzgerald's help via Mo Gale at the Savoy and not taking her into his band while playing Buffalo.
251.q: Which is another mistake. Another mistake is not taking Ella Fitzgerald in my band when I was playing at the Vendo. In New York? That's in New York? Oh, this was in New York, but not New York City. This was in Buffalo, New York. I was playing at the Vendo and at the Buffalo in Buffalo, New York.…

602.t: Ella Fitzgerald and Peg Leg Bates with Andy Kirk
602.s: With Andy Kirk, Gabriel travelled with Ella Fitzgerald and one-legged tap dancer Pegleg Bates.
602.q: Oh yes, well like that most of the fellas were doing for quite a while. Well, a lot of the arrangements from Offer Records, different bands were making because Ella Fitzgerald was out to see. She was in the band, her and Hot Lips and Pig Lake Bates was in the band when I played with Andy Kirk.…

84.t: Offers from big bands; brass band jobs
84.s: He got offers from Jimmy Lunceford among others and played a few brass band jobs.
84.q: Jam or anything? Oh yeah, I jam with him. Yeah. Oh yeah, I jam with him. When he coming out of the lyrics, the lyrics to you. Yeah, I jam with him. Did you ever get any offers from those guys? Yes, in my twenties I got a lot of offers. Who were some of the guys? Jimmy Lundford. I got offers from…

248.t: Working with Celestin and Emma Barrett
248.s: A few jobs with Celestin and many with Emma Barrett, including Brennan's.
248.q: I played a couple of jobs with Papa, but not to be in the band, you know, not regular, no. Did you ever work with Emma Barrett much? Emma? Sure, I worked with Emma a good many times.

119.t: One week with Ella Fitzgerald and the borrowed bass
119.s: He misses connecting with Ella's group by leaving his bass in a baggage room, then borrows a bass against his ring and plays a week with her.
119.q: I think I lost about, at that time I lost about ten or fifteen pounds. Of course today that would be great. But anyway that went on for a while and then I says I have to do something about this. I says it’s time for me to make a change. Because I’ve heard other people talking about that they needed…

224.t: Summer of 1952 with Hank Jones and Ella Fitzgerald
224.s: He played that summer behind Ella with Hank Jones and Nelson Boyd, still doing dates with Bird.
224.q: We weren’t based. We were working out of New York. I guess we really was based. But we were playing Michigan, Boston, Providence. I did the whole summer with them, ’52. Let’s see. ’52 or ’51? ’52. Yeah, because I still would have been doing little hits with Bird in between there.

114.t: Ella Fitzgerald holds the money; the stolen purse in Indianapolis
114.s: Ella kept money for Moody, Dave Burns and Joe Vail, and her purse was stolen in Indianapolis.
114.q: Oh, there were a lot of things like Ella Fitzgerald used to keep our money for us, me, Dave, and Joe Vail [phonetic sp.].

406.s: He got the job conducting Ella's band from Savoy owner Charlie Buchanan, ran rehearsals, enlarged the band and toured to California. The last job in 1942 was in Philadelphia with Bill Robinson before he went to ABC.
406.ch: Fletcher Henderson, Ella Fitzgerald and the early 1940s
406.q: And I come back and I worked with Don Redman in that era somewhere. Then finally one day I was down back of the Apollo Theater and I ran into Charlie Buchanan who had the Savoy. And he said, well, when are you going to come back and work for me. I said, well, I don't want to come back up there but…

382.t: Hearing Ella and John Kirby in Pittsburgh in 1932
382.s: She remembers promoting a dance near Homestead, Pennsylvania, where Ella's band played with John Kirby on bass.
382.ch: Early recordings and arrival in New York
382.q: I heard they were. So far, (inaudible) listen to recordings, you know, nine times out of ten everything that that particular person makes, they're going to like.

388.t: Illness ends his Shaw job; Buddy Rich takes over
388.s: Leeman is hospitalized for hemorrhoids and sent home to Maine; Shaw signs Buddy Rich, Glenn Miller calls, and he recalls Chick Webb and Ella next door at the Roseland.
388.q: But to get back to Artie Shaw, I became ill and it was just before Christmas at the Lincoln Hotel, and I had -- well, I don't mind telling you, I had a drummers occupational disease, hemorrhoids, and it was serious.

115.s: He was with Ella from 1956 to 1965, with a short spell in Woody Herman's small group in 1959, and she called him in Denver in 1973.
115.q: Yeah. I don't know whether she loved me or not, but when I first moved out here in '73, and she played her, well, they sent me a telegram, calling me.

75.t: Chick Webb's death and the Baltimore tribute
75.s: Soon after returning he played with Ella Fitzgerald's band, which took over after Chick Webb died, at the Baltimore stadium tribute.
75.ch: The war years: Barnet, Hot Lips Page, Newton and Kirby
75.q: Yeah, Chick Webb died, and the Ink Spots and Ella took the band over; she was the leader of the band. So they asked me to come and play with the band. Tommy Pulford, I think he was inducted into the Army as I remember, or he might have been ill -- I forget exactly. But I imagine he was inducted. So…
